svg.aria-label: How to write ജ: one unbroken stroke · 6 movements
svg.title: Writing ജ
svg.desc: 6 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of ജ (malayalam), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansMalayalam-Static.ttf. Stroke order after Rodney F. Moag, Malayalam: A University Course and Reference Grammar (University of Texas at Austin South Asia Institute and COERLL, updated April 2018; CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), Table IV 'How to Write Consonant Symbols', p. xxvi: movements 1-6 for ജ, written by hand by Thomas Joseph <https://github.com/matjic/malayalam/blob/7141acd2f310bc8928822a7aec61d1149efa6fa3/docs/assets/images/front-writing-036.jpg>. Source note on variation: Moag's Table IV (p. xxvi) circles the small top-left loop clockwise (1), arches over the left hump to the top of the short stem (2), climbs from the stem's foot and arches over the right hump (3), runs back down and left along the band to the lower left (4), runs right along the lower stroke to the top of the last loop (5) and rounds that loop clockwise, down its right side and up its left (6). Moag's arrows do not draw the short stem's descent: arrow 2 ends above the stem and arrow 3 begins at its foot. With no lift between them, the only way to the foot is down the stem, so the path runs down it at the end of movement 2 and climbs it again in movement 3; that join is read, not drawn, so confidence in it is medium. Moag's book is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, so only these facts (order, start, direction and end) are cited; no drawing is copied. The page is read from the scan in Mathew Jacob's digital edition (github.com/matjic/malayalam, commit 7141acd, and again at commit 2844253), which notes that the numbers mark drawing movements that can belong to one continuous stroke, not pen lifts. Santhosh Thottingal's hand reference curves (gitlab.com/santhoshtr/hand, MIT, 2019), which keep several strokes where a glyph has them, record ജ as one stroke from the upper left to the middle right. The grahyam online-handwriting samples (github.com/bluebottlewize/grahyam, no licence, cited as counts only) keep no pen-up marker, but none of the 45 unique samples jumps between consecutive points the way a lift would; they most often start at the upper left (27 of 45) and end at the middle right (27 of 45). SPACE Kerala's Thooval (GPL-3.0, facts only) starts its JA.png at the upper left and ends it at the lower right. The path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Malayalam outline rather than to Moag's drawing; the climb back up the stem and the run along the top of the last loop retrace ink already drawn.
svg.text: How it is written — one unbroken stroke · 6 movements
Stroke order after Rodney F. Moag, Malayalam: A University Course and Reference Grammar (University of Texas at Austin South Asia Institute and COERLL, updated April 2018; CC
BY-NC-SA 4.0), Table IV 'How to Write Consonant Symbols', p. xxvi: movements 1-6 for ജ, written by hand by Thomas Joseph
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
